messages:
maria: heads-up — seeing sustained stream of small batches that are keeping GPUs saturated and triggering admission backpressure. 99p latency for text-gen in us-west2 climbed to ~250ms. dashboard: https://internal.redwood/dashboard/rt/us-west2 :eyes:
luca: can you paste the admission + batcher metrics? curious if it's queue depth or kernel inefficiency causing the tail
maria: quick grab from the alert: admission_queue_depth spikes to 1200, batch_window_ms steady at 8, max_batch configured 32, average batch size ~6. GPUs at ~92% util. SLO is 99p < 200ms — failing for last 40m
ashley: this looks like continuous small-batch pressure. requests are steady but thinly spread so we flush often at the small batch size. that causes poor packing and forces the kernel into lots of tiny run() calls, which kills 99p
kevin: two knob ideas: increase batch_window_ms to allow more packing (e.g., 25ms) OR lower max_batch so we don't try to pack too many tiny sequences and thrash the KV cache. tradeoffs: window up -> slightly higher median but better 99p; lowering max_batch -> lower throughput.
maria: region impacted mostly: us-west2 pools gpu-pool-3 and gpu-pool-7. tail correlated with sequences >1024 tokens — creating KV-memory spikes and evictions
devops-bot: alert: host-pool-3 gpu-utilization high (0.92) | eviction_count +18 in last 10m | node restarts 0
luca: can we do a canary change? target one shard / pool and monitor 15m. If 99p drops then roll. can we patch runtime config via k8s configmap?
ashley: yeah, propose this experiment on pool-3 only:
```bash
kubectl -n infra patch configmap/batcher-config-pool-3 --type merge -p '{"data": {"batch_window_ms": "25", "max_batch": "20"}}'
```
start with batch_window_ms=25 and max_batch=20 for 15m. measure: admission_queue_depth, avg_batch_size, 99p latency, gpu_util
kevin: add monitoring snippet to query quickly:
```json
# quick prometheus
sum(rate(batch_flushes_total[1m])) by (pool)
```
also track kernel-run-duration histogram 99p
maria: launching canary on pool-3 now. will patch and report back. if it helps we can decide whether to prefer window increase vs max_batch cap
prio-oncall: FYI if canary helps we should avoid fleet-wide roll during peak — schedule roll in 10pm maintenance window. Also consider autoscaling more burst GPUs if this repeats
maria: patch applied at 1739152700. initial 5m look: avg_batch_size up to 11, admission_queue_depth down ~40%, 99p improved from 250ms -> 180ms so far. will keep monitoring for 15m
luca: great quick win. let's leave canary for 30m and then plan staged rollout. also file a follow-up postmortem note with data and decision rationale
ashley: next steps: 1) extend canary 30m 2) if stable, roll to all us-west2 pools with staged ramp 3) consider defaulting batch_window_ms to 20ms for high-latency buckets and add autotune rule based on avg_batch_size
kevin: also open action item to evaluate kernel behavior for many small flushes — long term might be a runtime optimization instead of config hacking
maria: noted. thanks all. :thumbsup:
